title: Reduce fixed-flag P104 junk from 45 to 44 with a signed split gather
body:
## Summary

This finite certificate gives a strict fixed-flag improvement for one P104
`C=56` source column. Across all ten legal single-gather schedules, the
minimum is 45 even off-diagonal junk entries. Replacing one gather by
`+2` at level 0 and `-1` at level 4 leaves 44. The full schedule preserves
104 diagonal entries and all 5,720 required odd off-diagonal zeros.

Credit DreamingOfClouds for the flag model, chain configuration and open
split-gather question in [#7689](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7689),
head `511e7d0852acdca291b50c538b978fb063ae7bac`. The new result is
the signed schedule and its exact comparison. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19718441)

## Evidence

Run from the repository root with CPython 3.12.15:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-c56-split-gather-witness
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/p104-c56-split-gather-witness --check-source-history
python3.12 -I -W error -B research/p104-c56-split-gather-witness/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/p104-c56-split-gather-witness/verify.py
```

Both verifier modes emit `PASS_P104_C56_SPLIT_GATHER_WITNESS`. The ten unsplit
schedules leave 45, 47 and 48 junk entries with multiplicities 2, 2 and 6.
The full replay checks the prescribed entries and rejects a late piece and
an incorrect coefficient total. Each verifier command took under one second
locally.

## Scope

The comparison fixes one set of eight flags, one read per chain and signed
rational gather pieces. The best split schedule, the optimum over all flags
and any implication for the multiplication exponent are open. This replay
covers the formal decoder. Physical gathers, restoration, a complete caller
invoice, selected cold replay and Lean were outside the verification.

## Open next questions

- Fix flags from a low-junk single-gather schedule and solve the per-column
  zero equations for signed prefix coefficients. This tests whether the gain
  persists near the global single-gather optimum.
- Price both gather pieces and their restoration on a fixed native carrier.
  The additional gather must cost less than the removed junk for a paid gain.

## Related open work

- [#7689](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7689) gives
  class-wide junk bounds with one gather and one read per chain.
- [#7659](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7659) uses
  a junk floor as a hypothesis in a conditional congestion ceiling.
- [#7668](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7668) gives
  tiered ceilings under distinct junk-count or decoder hypotheses.
- [#7678](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7678) refines
  the congestion ceiling for the frontier-word class on the same ports.
